subject: Onboarding request: aurora-mini-q4 variant + pin exception
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tasha Verma <tasha@aurorasoft.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Aurora-mini-q4 variant: onboarding + pin exception

Team —

Aurora (Tasha cc'd) has provided a compact variant they believe is a good fit for low-latency chat paths: aurora-mini-q4. Product would like to onboard it to the model catalog and request a version pin for the initial rollout. Quick context and asks: 

- Why: this variant is optimized for 2048 tokens with a q4 quantization profile; latency and cost look attractive compared to our current aurora-mini-q3 baseline.
- Primary ask: compatibility check + recommended pin_version (if necessary) so we can gate rollout without surprising regressions.
- Constraints: we need the model to be available in hosted and Dedicated pools in us-west-2 for the canary.

What I need from infra/research by EOD Monday:
- a short compatibility checklist (memory, KV cache behavior, kernel assumptions)
- quick eval on our smoke prompts (I attached a small sample set)
- recommendation on whether we should pin to a specific upstream release for the first 2 weeks

Tasha — thanks for the artifact drop earlier. If there are known caveats (context fragmentation, attention implementation differences), please call them out here.

Thanks — I'll coordinate rollout with ops once we have the green light.

— Mateo
Product Manager
Redwood Inference

> Team —
> 
> Aurora (Tasha cc'd) has provided a compact variant they believe is a good fit for low-latency chat paths: aurora-mini-q4.

Thanks Mateo — quick read here. I'm starting a compatibility pass; preliminary checklist below. I marked items we can answer immediately versus need artifacts/tests.

Immediate checks (I can run these):
- Peak GPU memory at max batch=8, seq_len=2048 (approx expected): estimate 18.5 GB for bf16 kernel, ~10.3 GB for q4 kernel.
- KV cache shape aligned with our runtime: K/V per layer = [batch, num_heads, seq_len, head_dim]. Looks standard.
- Supported attention type: standard causal; no flashing kernels required.

Needs artifacts/tests (please provide):
- Representative long-context prompts (>=1600 tokens) — I used sample_prompts.csv but need more edge cases for memory pressure.
- A model wheel with quantized kernels or a TorchScript artifact we can run through the profiling harness.
- Upstream model tag/version (we need SHA or release tag to recommend a pin).

Questions for research/runtime teams:
- Grace — do you see any known quality regressions on q4 profiles vs q8 for our eval families?
- Karthik — if we pin to a vendor tag, we should ensure CI/rollout automation can swap fallback to aurora-mini-q3 automatically; can you confirm runbook exists?

I'll attach the quick profiling output (work in progress) once I run the artifact through the harness.

Dev
Infra — Serving Runtime

Attachments: onboard-rollout-checklist.md (stub)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tasha Verma <tasha@aurorasoft.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora-mini-q4 variant: onboarding + pin exception

Dev — thanks. I ran the initial eval sweep against our primary prompt families (chat, few-shot instruction, long-context summarization). Summary highlights below; full report attached.

Executive summary:
- Short-context (<=512 tokens): aurora-mini-q4 closely matches aurora-mini-q3 in F1/ROUGE and human-rated helpfulness.
- Long-context (>1200 tokens): we observed a small but systematic degradation on chain-of-thought style prompts (precision down ~4-6 points vs q3) for reasoning tasks that depend on long-range attention.
- Safety: no new safety categories triggered in the sweep, but a small uptick in hallucination rate on condensed summarization tasks under q4 quantization.

Recommendation:
- Pin recommendation: pin to aurora-mini-q4@v20260715-quant for the initial canary. That tag corresponds to the vendor release with the q4 quantization script we evaluated. Pin duration: 14 days.
- Rollout gating: require A/B monitoring on the long-context eval set and a quality alert threshold (delta F1 > 3 points or hallucination rate +2%) to pause rollout.
- Fallback: automatic fallback to aurora-mini-q3 if the quality threshold is exceeded; document rollout in JIRA INF-4823.

I've attached the full eval PDF (eval_report_aurora-mini-q4.pdf) with examples and the exact prompt set used. If Infra needs different artifacts (e.g., per-layer activation dumps) let me know and I can re-run.

Grace
Research — Model Quality

Attachments: eval_report_aurora-mini-q4.pdf

Thanks everyone — clear and helpful. Per Grace's recommendation I want to move forward with the following plan and request an official pin-exception for the catalog entry so ops can lock the initial canary to the vendor tag.

Planned rollout (high level):
- Week 0: Onboard aurora-mini-q4@v20260715-quant to staging, run canary with 5% traffic in us-west-2 hosted; run identical canary in a small Dedicated pool.
- Week 1: Expand to 20% if quality metrics hold; continuous monitoring on long-context eval family.
- Week 2: Remove pin (or extend) depending on quality delta and Aurora's follow-up patch cadence.

Action items assigned: 
- Dev: full compatibility run (memory, perf, fallback behavior) + confirm that canary fallback to aurora-mini-q3 is automated and tested. Please attach profiling artifacts to JIRA INF-4823.
- Grace: publish a one-page gating doc with the exact thresholds and examples to post to the runbook.
- Karthik: prepare the catalog change with pin metadata and the rollout policy; request formal approval from Laura for the pin exception.

Laura — can you approve a catalog pin exception for 14 days (v20260715-quant) so we can proceed? If approved, Karthik will mark the change and ops will schedule the canary next Wednesday.

Tasha — thanks for collating the release tag. Please stand by in case infra needs an artifact or a patch.

— Mateo
Product Manager
Redwood Inference
